mstts:express-as.prosody:
Let’s talk about something that’s both tough and all too real— living with unapologized wrongs.
Not every story wraps up with that perfect ending, where someone says they’re sorry and everything’s made right again. Sometimes, those words just never come. Maybe the person who hurt you isn’t willing to apologize. Maybe they can’t. Or maybe, they’re simply not around anymore.
And that’s when the pain can linger, isn’t it? It almost feels like a second wound—a refusal to even recognize what you’ve been through. You might find yourself replaying what happened, hoping for words that just aren’t coming. It’s easy to get stuck in that loop.
But here’s something to remember: healing is still possible, even when you don’t get the apology you deserve. Some people find comfort by talking things out with friends, or by writing down their feelings. Others turn to a counselor for support. Sometimes, the real shift happens when you choose to forgive—not for them, but for yourself.
Letting go of anger can be a way to take back your power. It’s a choice to put peace above bitterness, even when it feels unfair.
And closure doesn’t always have to come from the other person. Sometimes, offering your own apology, even if it’s just for your part in what happened, can bring a sense of relief. Saying, “I’m sorry for my part in this,” can be freeing—even if no one else ever acknowledges it. Taking responsibility for your actions—no matter how small—can help you move forward.
Living with unapologized wrongs isn’t easy. It takes a lot of courage, and a whole lot of patience. You have to be willing to accept what you can’t change. But you know what? You really can move forward. You can build new relationships, and find joy again.
The absence of an apology doesn’t have to define your story.
